stem: A factory spills oil into a bay, polluting it beyond the allowed standards. Under Section 16 of RA 9275, who is responsible for cleaning it up?
choices: The factory, at its own expense
The DENR, using only public funds
The city where the bay is located
The fishers who use the bay
answer: The factory, at its own expense
hints: The Clean Water Act follows the idea that whoever causes pollution must answer for it.
Section 16, "Clean-Up Operations," begins its rule with "any person who causes pollution ..."
Section 16 also covers emergencies: if the DENR has to do the clean-up, the expenses "shall be reimbursed" by someone. Check who pays in the end, then compare the choices.

solution.methodName: Apply the rule to the facts

steps.action: Recall Section 16 of RA 9275: "any person who causes pollution in or pollutes water bodies in excess of the applicable and prevailing standards shall be responsible to contain, remove and clean-up any pollution incident at his own expense."
Apply it to the facts: the factory caused the spill, so the factory must clean it up and pay for it.
Check the emergency rule: if the polluter fails to act, the DENR may do the clean-up, but the expenses "shall be reimbursed by the persons found to have caused such pollution."
steps.why: So even then, the cost goes back to the polluter, not to the public.

steps.action: The answer is the factory, at its own expense.

trapNotes.The DENR, using only public funds: The DENR steps in only if the polluter fails to act in an emergency, and the polluter must pay the costs back.
trapNotes.The city where the bay is located: LGUs help with emergency response (Section 20), but Section 16 puts the clean-up and its cost on whoever caused the pollution.
trapNotes.The fishers who use the bay: The fishers did not cause the spill. The law makes the polluter responsible.
